findings.original_assumption: Lemma 3.5 is stated for good edges in the leading channels: compatible dependent regular pairs, with private prime coordinates on their distinct normalized values. It gives a rank lower bound with O(1), a width O(B) and B^{O(1)} endpoint patterns.
findings.finding: Finite compression holds for arbitrary positive coprime coefficients a<=b as soon as one normalized value is shared and the distinct normalized values have private parity coordinates. Affine compatibility, dependence, physical separation and a prior local-regularity assumption are unnecessary. Private coordinates already imply both local ranks equal L. The actual compressed rank is |U|-1 and at least (2-1/b)*L-1. There are at most (L+1)^2 fixed integer motifs, all in [-bL,bL]; one fixed-pattern integer anchor determines both centres. The private-value intersection now has an explicit coefficient classification: space(S) intersect space(T)=space(S intersect T), and even coefficients on the true intersection are linearly equivalent to the actual common class space. Actual normalized units are bijective with the deduplicated intersection values. For positive a,b and centres at least two, even selections of the actual units are therefore linearly equivalent to S_x intersect S_y; its rank and the full pair deficiency both equal (u-1)_+, including zero and one unit. Coprimality, alignment height, separation and affine compatibility are unnecessary for this private-intersection classification. The actual affine character of an even true-window selection is its predecessor coefficient. For even exact-unit coefficients, the paired character is the sign of the sum of the two predecessor parities. Full-support pair relations are explicitly reindexed by nonzero actual common classes. For a private normalized pair with positive length, each marginal is proved to equal p=2^-L, and the actual covariance equals p^2 times the signed nonzero even-unit sum. No joint compatibility, separation, coprimality or alignment height is imposed; probability-zero pairs retain their character cancellations.
findings.proposed_revision: State the finite compression for positive coprime coefficients a<=b, a shared normalized value and private coordinates, and then specialize to good edges. Replace the unspecified finite losses and offset count by rank >=(2-1/b)*L-1 and at most (L+1)^2 motifs in [-bL,bL]. State explicitly that the anchor determines both centres and that local regularity follows from the private-coordinate condition. State the exact private-intersection coefficient equivalence and rank identities separately, including zero and one exact unit. Keep the shared-value premise for the full union-compression image identity; the zero-unit intersection result does not remove that premise. Give the actual predecessor characters and private pair covariance with separately chosen local affine witnesses; retain probability-zero pairs and require distinct centres for the two-element event.
findings.impact: Gives explicit finite compression constants, motifs and anchor uniqueness, derives local regularity from privacy, and classifies actual private common classes by even exact-unit coefficients including zero and one unit. Actual predecessor characters and private pair covariance are proved without joint compatibility, separation, coprimality or height restrictions. Full union-image compression still requires a shared value. The subsequent MATH-0045 completes the actual fixed-channel mass T2.5. The complete main pair profile and optimality remain separate unfinished claims.

The full old square-class span is used. The uniform count of all actual lists admitting nonempty even short motifs is proved for arbitrary fixed polylogarithmic new widths and arbitrary finite centre subsets of each fixed comparable positive range. The old character density is nonnegative, has mean one and exact positive real moments; its Holder cost is bounded by (2^|O|)^(r/v). A sufficiently large fixed even v absorbs this cost, and the proved actual 9.1 Lp estimate then fixes c>0 before every fixed interval/width constant. Every actual motif and projected tuple is counted, with repetitions retained. No enumeration of the old 2^dim classes is needed in the estimate.
findings.proposed_revision: State the old-space projection result for any finite generator set of size O(logN), or equivalently any finitely generated old space with the corresponding dimension bound, without requiring old-block diameter or height control. Retain the source block version as a corollary via the cardinality of the union. Allow fixed polylogarithmic new widths as in P1-MATH-0059. Display the exact old-density moments and Holder cost (2^|O|)^(r/v), and specify that c is chosen before interval and width constants.

findings.original_assumption: Companion Lemma T6.1 fixes q>0, uses blocks of logarithmic width B, and chooses H=C_D*B larger than the block diameters. Its bound is stated with constants depending on q.
findings.finding: The actual centre count is at most Q*N^epsilon for any nonnegative real product cap Q, with one threshold before Q and all varying cutoffs, offsets and centre families. The cutoff only needs H<=D*logN and need not exceed the block diameter; the offset width can be any fixed polylogarithm. Actual large kernels individually have polynomial height derived from the centre interval. Grouping positive kernel pairs by their product and injecting each fibre into divisors gives Q*N^eta uniformly in Q. Actual small-prime supports have uniformly subpolynomial choices, and each resulting pair of full linear kernels has a proved subpolynomial Pell fibre, including the factorizable case. Finite offset and interval covers are summed. Consequently the q formulation is uniform for every real q after the same threshold, even if q varies with N.
findings.proposed_revision: State the stronger Q*N^epsilon count with a threshold independent of the real cap Q>=0. Retain N^(q+epsilon) as a corollary, allowing real q to vary. Separate the logarithmic cutoff from the fixed polylogarithmic offset width, and remove the unused condition H>block diameter from this lemma. Explain that polynomial actual kernel heights make the divisor bound uniform in Q.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T6.2 asks for more than c*loglogN selected values and uses entire Y-smooth parts, large-prime square parts and a first-passage modulus with prime-power multiplicities. The surrounding setup takes H above the block diameter.
findings.finding: Only t+26 distinct selected values are needed. One uses the full canonical square part and the squarefree Y-small odd-prime part instead of the entire smooth part. Outside the two-small-kernel exception at H, at most one selected value has full square part squared exceeding N^(19/25); after removing it and fewer than t large Y-kernels, 26 parts remain, each at least a fixed positive multiple of N^(1/25). Their lcm exceeds the centre interval using a proved pairwise-gcd product estimate. Its squarefree prime union admits a squarefree first-passage modulus m between the interval height X and X*Y. Actual coprime prime allocations give a literal congruence certificate. The deterministic exceptional set is counted by proved Rankin, divisor, offset and congruence bounds. It is independent of t, H and the selection, and the constant-selection threshold precedes every varying t and H. No condition H>diameter or H<=Y is used. findings.proposed_revision: Replace the long-selection hypothesis by cardinality at least t+26 in the smooth-modulus lemma, retaining the long-selection formulation as a corollary. State that the deterministic exceptional set can be chosen independently of t and H, and that the construction does not require H to exceed the block diameter.

findings.original_assumption: Main Lemma 14.2 proves D(u,v,w)<=19/30 on primitive integer triples u<v<w<2u and gives equality at (10,12,15), without asserting uniqueness or the next possible overlap value.
findings.finding: The extremal primitive ordered triple is unique: D=19/30 if and only if (u,v,w)=(10,12,15). Every other primitive ordered triple in the source range has D<=11/18, and (8,9,12) attains that value. Thus canonical coincidence geometry has the sharp gap 19/30-11/18=1/45. The proof treats every possible low reduced-height pair, retains the actual gcd formula, and proves all finite numerator/denominator exclusions. Integer positivity and the passage to natural slopes are proved from the printed hypotheses. On actual private rational triples with zero affine intercept, the gap now gives point-probability exponents -71/30 and -43/18 uniformly at every primitive slope height, and literal host mass bounds N^(-41/30+epsilon) and N^(-25/18+epsilon) at polynomial logarithmic slope height. General intercept and nonprivate sectors are not asserted. The actual rational probability and host-mass consequences extend from raw private normalized values to full even-selection rank, a strictly weaker condition invariant under common positive dilation. All zero-intercept primitive rational triples of slope height bounded before N satisfy the actual probability and mass gap without private, even-injective or regular-window filters: the entire merged-value kernel is proved O_Q(B/log B). For Q>=15 the exponent 41/30 is attained by the actual extremal witness population. The even-rank polynomial-height sector has a checked nonextremal relative-mass decay N^(-1/45+epsilon). The finite canonical loss bound now holds for arbitrary independent window translations with absolute error 3. Under connected normalized overlap and full even rank, the actual probability gap is uniform in all translations and slope heights, without a predecessor-exclusivity premise. The finite canonical bound now combines with the already proved actual target-union residual to give unconditional point probability N^(-71/30+epsilon) and literal host mass N^(-41/30+epsilon) for all distinct interior physical slopes above one fixed reduced source channel, with arbitrary affine offsets and polynomial target height B^J. No private, even-injective, regular-window or connected-normalized-overlap hypothesis is imposed. Repeated physical, endpoint and nonaligned sectors remain open.
findings.proposed_revision: Strengthen Lemma 14.2 by adding the equality classification and the sharp bound D<=11/18 away from (10,12,15), with the witness (8,9,12). Keep the statement restricted to primitive ordered triples in the strict ratio range. Explicitly retain the existing distinction between canonical coincidence geometry and additional arithmetic relations among distinct normalized values. Add the checked private zero-intercept probability and mass consequence, with explicit finite rank error 5 and the inherited 1/45 exponent gap.

findings.original_assumption: Step 1 states freeness of the original coordinate algebra over the plane and finiteness and birationality of its radical-sum projection; it does not give a free power basis for the actual image algebra.
findings.finding: The actual affine image R[s], where s is the sum of the independent radicals, is itself a finite free R-module of rank 2^k, with literal basis 1,s,...,s^(2^k-1). Its single monic irreducible equation is the actual minimal polynomial of s, has Z-degree 2^k, and generates the full evaluation kernel. The general proof requires only a domain R with characteristic-zero fraction field and actual generic radicand independence. In addition, one fixed integer-coefficient polynomial in the k formal radicands and the sum variable specializes to every actual independent system. Its total degree C(k) gives totalDegree(H)<=C(k)*max(1,K), a coefficient-independent upper bound linear in the maximum root-list degree K.
findings.proposed_revision: After the finite birational projection argument, give the presentation R[s]=R[Z]/(P), with P monic of Z-degree 2^k, and state the resulting power basis and free rank of the actual image over the plane. Distinguish this base projection from the finite birational source-to-image morphism. Describe the fixed universal polynomial and record the bound C(k)*max(1,K) in place of the unspecified dependence on K in the defining-polynomial degree upper bound.
findings.impact: Strengthens the algebraic description of the projected image and makes its defining equation and generic degree explicit. Scalar-compatible formal-branch matching and binary separation at the remaining coordinates force every regular fibre root to the equation's own offset; actual separability proves the plane equation has Y-degree one. Constructed critical-equation deletion costs at most deg_X(C)+2 deg_X(C)deg_Y(C) equations. With both partial degrees and actual extension degree <=E and at least 4(E+1)^2 equations, an actual family of at least 2E+1 equations supplies actual integer curve matches. This works for even as well as odd cover degrees and takes no genus, Riemann--Hurwitz or common-quotient premise. The graph-forcing result is now connected through an actual reduced rational presentation to the complete uniform critical-band exclusion for the stated nonconstant-coordinate bounded-cover data, for arbitrary finite cover degree. The actual coefficient denominator is proved nonzero at every actual integer curve point by irreducibility; canonical reduction cannot increase degree and preserves actual curve points and offset matches. Positive reduced degree is derived from an actual offset match and host positivity.
